attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his voice as "I am certain".

semantics.note: "I am certain" plus "is going to" is unqualified, high-confidence language, so it is a scorable forecast. The normalisation keeps the target, the vague horizon ("near future"), the cause (thousands of people using AI coding tools) and both compounding factors (layoffs and busywork culture).

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. It sets no calendar deadline for "near future", does not count earlier incidents, and requires the causal chain the speaker himself named. Failing to find a qualifying incident does not count against him because he gave no deadline. The result does not depend on any contested reading.

evidence.note: GitHub's own account of an outage after publication (Aug 17, 2026, about 7h47m). It blames network saturation, a misconfigured autoscaling policy and retry bugs. Nothing links it to AI-assisted development at scale, layoffs, or busywork culture, so it does not fulfil the forecast.
Amazon's statement about its own retail incidents from before the March 2026 article. They happened before publication, so they cannot fulfil or refute the forecast.

Aggregate vendor survey (July–August 2026) reporting AI-coding-related incidents across organisations. It names no major big-tech service failure and gives no causal findings, so it is only background.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. No item in the packet documents a failure after publication that meets the full chain: a major big-tech service breaks, is not quickly fixed, and AI-assisted development by thousands of people, layoffs and busywork culture are shown to have caused or worsened it. The GitHub outage had other documented causes. Because there is no deadline, the absence of such an incident does not contradict the forecast.
